skill.name: spawn
skill.description: Spawn external coding agents and CLI commands in separate terminal sessions with optional output capture.
skill.summary: Launch coding agents or terminal commands in separate sessions and capture their output when needed.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Static analysis correctly identified real command execution and temporary file risks in fork_terminal.py. Many Markdown backtick and documentation matches are false positives, but the skill still has high risk because it spawns unrestricted commands and recommends automatic approval modes. No evidence found of prompt injection text or malicious credential exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: Raw command strings are passed into shell and terminal interpreter contexts.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer argument arrays, allowlisted commands, and explicit user confirmation before execution. Avoid shell=True unless a reviewed shell command is required.

remediation.issue: Agent cookbooks recommend approval bypass or force modes.
remediation.suggestion: Make sandboxed or confirmation-based modes the default. Move dangerous modes behind explicit warnings and user opt-in.

remediation.issue: Captured output and generated scripts are written under temporary directories.
remediation.suggestion: Use securely created temporary files with private permissions, clean them up after use, and warn users when outputs may contain secrets.

remediation.issue: Conversation summaries may be forwarded to spawned agents.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for consent before forwarding conversation history and redact secrets, credentials, file paths, and private business data.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Shell Command Execution Path
semantic_findings.description: fork_terminal accepts a raw command string and several platform branches execute it through shell or terminal command contexts. This is intentional for the skill, but it exposes the user system to arbitrary local command execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The function signature takes command as a string and the fallback path executes it with shell=True. The behavior is explicit and security-sensitive even though it matches the skill purpose.

semantic_findings.title: Approval and Sandbox Bypass Defaults
semantic_findings.description: The Codex and Cursor cookbooks recommend automatic or forced execution modes. These defaults reduce user review before spawned agents edit files or run commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly recommend dangerous bypass or force modes. The exact impact depends on the installed CLI, but the documented intent is automatic approval.

semantic_findings.title: Conversation History Forwarding to Spawned Agents
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the assistant to place conversation history into a prompt for a spawned agent. This can disclose sensitive user context to another CLI or provider if not confirmed and redacted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prompt template and workflow explicitly include conversation summaries for a forked agent. This is useful functionality, but it creates a clear data exposure risk.

content.value_statement: Developers often need interactive agents or long-running CLI tasks without blocking their main session. This skill opens terminal sessions for coding agents and generic commands while documenting output capture.
actual_capabilities: Launch Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, or Copilot agents in a new terminal.
Run generic CLI commands in a separate terminal session.
Capture clean agent output or debug terminal output to temporary files.
Read captured output after a spawned command completes.
Open provider authentication commands in a terminal when login is required.
limitations: It executes powerful local commands and requires careful user review.
It depends on installed CLI tools and each tool authentication state.
Output capture uses temporary files, so sensitive prompts may appear on disk.
Windows and WSL capture behavior can vary by terminal setup.

use_cases.title: Run Long CLI Jobs
use_cases.description: Open a separate terminal for build, media, or package commands while the main assistant continues working.

use_cases.title: Launch Interactive Coding Agents
use_cases.description: Start a selected AI coding CLI with a prompt, model choice, and optional captured output.

use_cases.title: Handle Provider Login Flows
use_cases.description: Open a terminal for provider authentication when a coding CLI needs browser or interactive login.
use_cases.target_user: Tool maintainers setting up agent credentials

prompt_templates.title: Open a Build Terminal
prompt_templates.prompt: Use spawn-terminal to open a new terminal and run npm run build. Check the command help or package script first.

prompt_templates.title: Start Claude Code Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use spawn-agent with Claude Code to review the current bug report. Keep permissions conservative and return the output path.

prompt_templates.title: Run Codex with Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Use spawn-agent with Codex. Include a concise summary of our current task, then ask it to inspect the failing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Agent Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn separate agents for Codex and Cursor to investigate the performance regression. Capture clean outputs and summarize disagreements.

output_examples.input: Spawn a terminal for a long video conversion.
output_examples.output: A new terminal opens for the command. The assistant reports whether debug output is captured and where to find it.

output_examples.input: Start Codex to review the failing test suite.
output_examples.output: The skill selects the Codex cookbook, builds the CLI command, opens a terminal, and returns the captured output path.

output_examples.input: Open a login flow for Cursor Agent.
output_examples.output: A terminal opens for the Cursor authentication command. The caller waits for the login flow to finish or time out.

best_practices: Review every command before spawning it in a terminal.
Prefer sandboxed or confirmation-based agent modes for untrusted prompts.
Delete captured output files when they may contain sensitive data.
anti_patterns: Do not run untrusted prompts with approval bypass or full system access.
Do not pass secrets in prompts, command arguments, or captured output files.
Do not use this skill for simple commands that can run safely in the current session.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It opens new terminal sessions for AI coding agents or generic CLI commands.

faq.question: Which agents are documented?
faq.answer: The skill documents Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and Copilot command patterns.

faq.question: Can it capture output?
faq.answer: Yes. It can write clean agent output or debug terminal output to temporary files.

faq.question: Does it install the CLI tools?
faq.answer: No. The required CLI tools and credentials must already exist on the user system.

faq.question: Why is this skill security sensitive?
faq.answer: It launches external processes and some cookbooks recommend powerful automatic approval modes.

faq.question: How should users reduce risk?
faq.answer: Users should prefer sandboxed modes, verify commands, avoid secrets, and remove temporary output files.
